articles.title: Webb Captures Stars in the Early Stages of Life in a Nearby Stellar Nursery
articles.description: This Webb infrared image, released on October 6th, 2026, shows the star-forming region NGC 7129, about 3,300 light-years from Earth. The central star, LkHα 234, is a young star of 5–8 solar masses whose outflows have cleared a cavity about 3.5 light-years across. On the right side of the region, younger protostars shoot jets of very hot material that create shocks in the surrounding gas.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captured stunning infrared images of NGC 7129, a nearby stellar nursery 3,300 light-years away, revealing stars in their earliest stages of formation.

articles.title: Webb image reveals young stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description: In this Picture of the Month from the NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope, we visit a turbulent cauldron of star formation to see what is brewing inside dense clumps of gas. This is a star-forming region named LHA 120-N 159, or simply N159, located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This image spans about 230 light-years across.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A stunning James Webb Space Telescope image showcases a turbulent star-forming region where young stars are actively brewing within a nebulous cauldron of gas and dust.

articles.title: Supermassive black holes ejected from galactic centers? Quasar survey supports decade-old prediction
articles.description: By analyzing data on around 100,000 quasars, or extremely luminous galactic nuclei, researchers at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) have found statistical evidence that some supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies are ejected from their positions after forming. The relationship now identified in the data was predicted 10 years ago by members of the same research group, Peter Raffai and Zsolt Frei, together with Zoltán Haiman.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of approximately 100,000 quasars provides strong evidence supporting a decade-old prediction that supermassive black holes can be ejected from galactic centers.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has shattered a historic space exploration record, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it. Its advanced self-driving system helped it surpass Opportunity’s 28.06-mile record in just five and a half years, a feat that previously took nearly 15. Now, Perseverance is exploring some of the oldest rocks in the solar system, searching for clues about ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has broken the all-time off-world driving record, traveling farther across Mars than any previous rover. This milestone demonstrates the mission's continued success and scientific productivity.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
articles.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.
articles.summary: Astronomers have achieved a major breakthrough by measuring conditions during the Universe's first five minutes after the Big Bang. This discovery deepens our understanding of the cosmos' earliest and most fundamental moments.

articles.title: NASA giving update about Artemis moon plans on Oct. 23: Watch it live
articles.description: NASA will provide an update about its Artemis III mission and its plans to land astronauts on the moon during a press conference on Friday (Oct. 23). Here's how to watch it live.
articles.summary: NASA will provide an update on its Artemis III mission plans to land astronauts on the moon during a press conference on October 23rd. This landmark announcement represents a major milestone in humanity's return to lunar exploration.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen wins the 2026 Physics Nobel Prize for his vision that grew into the IceCube observatory, which detects high-energy neutrinos from the cosmos. This achievement represents a major breakthrough in observational astronomy and fundamental physics.

articles.title: NASA’s Hubble Charts Path for Roman with Gravitational Lenses
articles.description: This observation is one of many gravitational lensing images taken by Hubble in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope is charting gravitational lensing observations to prepare for science operations with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, advancing our ability to study distant galaxies and cosmology.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 October 22 – The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 22 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The First […]
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered WD J1330+6435, the first known green star, a rare white dwarf with unique atmospheric properties that challenge our understanding of stellar composition.

articles.title: NASA Conducts RS-25 Engine Test in Support of Future Artemis Missions
articles.description: NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Test teams fired the developmental engine for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During […]
articles.summary: NASA successfully tested the RS-25 engine at Stennis Space Center in preparation for future Artemis lunar missions that will return humans to the Moon.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Ninety years later, the lab, now managed by Caltech for NASA, isn’t […]
articles.summary: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory looks toward the next 90 years of innovation, envisioning interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Martian helicopters as part of humanity's exploration future.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully lifts off to explore Phobos, Mars's mysterious moon, opening new frontiers in planetary science.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: The BepiColombo mission celebrates a significant anniversary as it continues its groundbreaking journey to explore Mercury and unlock the secrets of the innermost planet.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's capability to uncover new solar system objects.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch aboard Japan's H3 rocket to study Mars's enigmatic moons and advance our understanding of the Mars system.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Solar Orbiter has tracked the origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, solving a key puzzle in solar physics.

articles.title: Even the Rubin's Test Camera Produces Stunning Images
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory's Commissioning Camera operated for about 7 weeks in 2024, before the observatory released its well-known first look images. It's an engineering camera, and its job was to test the VRO's equipment and procedures. Now, the VRO has released the ComCam's image of the Seagull nebula. It's a pretty stunning image for an engineering camera.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory's Commissioning Camera produced remarkable images during its 7-week 2024 operation, demonstrating the observatory's exceptional imaging capabilities before the main instrument deployment.

articles.title: Two Disks in One: How Accretion Disks Drive Black Hole Jets
articles.description: SMBH jets are driven by thick, hot accretion disks with powerful magnetic fields. But there's a bit of a paradox. Some SMBH produce jets, even though they appear to have thin, cold accretion disks. New research has solved this paradox, showing that disks can be truncated into an outer cold disk and an inner hot disk.
articles.summary: New research reveals how thick, hot accretion disks with powerful magnetic fields drive jets from supermassive black holes, resolving a key paradox in black hole physics.

articles.title: New Evidence for an Old Prediction: Recoiling Supermassive Black Holes
articles.description: Theory says that during some SMBH mergers, the merger remnant receives a recoil kick from gravitational waves. Instead of sitting placidly in the galactic center, these recoiled SMBH are sent on a pendulum-like motion, back and forth through the galactic center. New research has found statistical evidence supporting their existence.
articles.summary: Observational evidence supports the decades-old theoretical prediction that supermassive black hole mergers produce recoil kicks from gravitational waves, causing the merger remnant to move through space.

articles.title: Supernova Explosions First Aided, Then Later Impeded, the Epoch of Reionization
articles.description: The Epoch of Reionization is when radiation from early galaxies and their stars reionized neutral hydrogen and let light travel freely through the cosmos. Some research shows that supernovae helped the process. But new research shows that, though they may have helped initially, supernovae eventually slowed reionization.
articles.summary: Research reveals the complex role supernova explosions played in the Epoch of Reionization, first promoting then impeding the reionization of the universe's neutral hydrogen.

articles.title: Black hole observations uncover evidence of solar storm–like magnetic eruptions
articles.description: Technion researchers have presented evidence for the existence of solar-storm-like outbursts near supermassive black holes, which can be a million times larger than the sun or more. The phenomenon was discovered in the vicinity of the black hole in the galaxy NGC 3783, and the researchers' findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Technion researchers have identified evidence of solar-storm-like magnetic eruptions occurring in the vicinity of supermassive black holes, expanding our understanding of black hole behavior.

articles.title: Are 'mega-Earths' real? Stellar activity may explain these oversized rocky worlds
articles.description: A new study suggests that some of the heaviest rocky planets ever reported may not be as heavy as they look. These so-called 'mega-Earths,' rocky planets weighing more than about 10 Earths, could be an illusion created by activity on their host stars. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 8.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New research suggests some of the heaviest rocky planets may have been overestimated in mass due to stellar activity effects. This discovery refines our understanding of mega-Earth exoplanets and their true characteristics.

articles.title: NASA’s Curiosity rover reveals a spectacular new view of Mars with a mystery on the horizon
articles.description: NASA’s Curiosity rover has revealed a spectacular new view of mysterious, wind-carved cliffs on Mars that may hold evidence of ancient volcanic activity. With the rover approaching these unusual formations, scientists hope to uncover the secrets behind their strange appearance in 2027.
articles.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover captured spectacular imagery of wind-carved cliffs on Mars that may contain evidence of ancient geological processes. The discovery offers new insights into Mars' geological history and habitability.

articles.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
articles.description: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight. Researchers found that astronauts' hearts adapted to months of weightlessness and handled simulated Martian gravity without major problems, offering new hope for future missions to the Red Planet.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking study of 13 astronauts reveals that the human heart may be well-adapted for long-duration space travel to Mars. This encouraging finding advances our understanding of human physiology for deep space exploration.

articles.title: NASA solves a strange mystery hidden inside asteroid Bennu’s boulders
articles.description: NASA scientists have finally uncovered why asteroid Bennu loses heat so quickly despite being covered in massive boulders. Samples returned to Earth reveal that its rocks are filled with hidden cracks, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years.
articles.summary: NASA scientists have uncovered the mystery of why asteroid Bennu rapidly loses heat despite its boulder-covered surface. This discovery enhances our knowledge of asteroid thermal properties and composition.

articles.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
articles.description: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.
articles.summary: NASA presents a stunning gallery of 16 galaxies featuring colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and dramatic cosmic phenomena. The images reveal the universe's most violent and energetic processes.

articles.title: Astronomers discover a ghostly green star unlike any known before
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered a surprising rainbow of dead stars, including the first known star that would appear genuinely green to human eyes. Researchers found that white dwarfs can glow in unexpected shades of pink, purple, yellow, and cyan because of unusual chemical interactions in their extremely dense atmospheres.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a rare ghostly green star unlike any previously known stellar object. This unprecedented find expands our knowledge of stellar diversity and exotic stellar phenomena.

articles.title: 'Cabin leak suspected': Artemis II astronaut reveals how a warning nearly derailed NASA's epic moon mission
articles.description: Victor Glover recalls how a suspected cabin leak warning came just 15 minutes before a crucial engine burn — and why receiving it just five minutes later could have changed everything.
articles.summary: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover recalls how a suspected cabin leak warning emerged just before a critical engine burn but was successfully resolved. This account highlights NASA's rigorous safety protocols and problem-solving during the historic moon mission.

articles.title: A Quantum Cyclotron for Antimatter
articles.description: Author(s): Paolo CrivelliA device that stores a single positron and controls its quantum states could measure its magnetic moment with unprecedented precision, testing a symmetry principle central to quantum field theory.[Physics 19, 132] Published Wed Oct 21…
articles.summary: A quantum cyclotron device can store and control a single positron to measure its magnetic properties with unprecedented precision. This breakthrough in antimatter research opens new possibilities for fundamental physics understanding.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar, expanding our understanding of these powerful cosmic objects. This discovery provides new insights into extreme astrophysical phenomena beyond traditional blazars.
